logical_components.title: CreateUserData
logical_components.description: Pydantic data model used as the request body schema for admin-created user creation. It defines five required string fields to validate incoming data before business logic executes: email, password, plan, first_name, last_name.
logical_components.business_logic: Acts as a Data Transfer Object (DTO) to validate payloads for admin-created user creation. Ensures proper typing and presence before hashing the password and persisting the user.

logical_components.title: CreateAdminData
logical_components.description: Pydantic data model used as the request body schema for creating a new admin (superuser) via admin routes. Fields mirror CreateUserData (email, password, plan, first_name, last_name).
logical_components.business_logic: Provides a minimal, validated contract for creating admin accounts. Facilitates automatic OpenAPI schema generation and input validation for admin creation workflows.

logical_components.title: UpdateUserPlanData
logical_components.description: Pydantic model representing the payload to update a user’s subscription plan via an admin route.
logical_components.business_logic: Enforces presence and type of user_id and plan; sets up data for downstream plan-update operations (potentially with an Enum-constrained plan in extended versions).

logical_components.title: UpdateUserTotalScansData
logical_components.description: Pydantic model for updating a user’s total_scans counter through an admin route.
logical_components.business_logic: Provides user_id and total_scans as required fields; validates payloads so downstream services can apply the new counter value.

logical_components.title: ToggleAdminAccessData
logical_components.description: Pydantic model for toggling a user’s admin privileges by user_id.
logical_components.business_logic: Serves as a minimal input contract to identify the target user; actual is_superuser state transition is implemented in route/service logic with proper authorization checks.

logical_components.title: Check Superuser Endpoint
logical_components.description: GET /admin/check_superuser endpoint that verifies whether the currently authenticated user is a superuser.
logical_components.business_logic: Resolves the current user from the Authorization header and enforces is_superuser. Returns a success payload (e.g., message, user_id, email) if authorized; returns HTTP 403 otherwise and handles DB errors with HTTP 500 when applicable.

logical_components.title: Admin Users List Endpoint
logical_components.description: Endpoint that returns a list of all users to an authenticated superuser.
logical_components.business_logic: Opens a DB session, queries all User records, maps them to simplified dicts (id, email, first_name, last_name, plan, is_superuser, total_scans), and returns the collection. Enforces 403 for non-admins and 500 for DB/unexpected errors.

logical_components.title: Admin Create User Endpoint
logical_components.description: POST /admin/create_user endpoint that creates a new non-admin user from admin-provided data.
logical_components.business_logic: Validates requester is a superuser, validates data.plan against predefined plans, checks for duplicate email, hashes the plaintext password, constructs a new User (is_superuser=False, total_scans=0), persists it, and commits. May trigger a welcome email and returns the new user details. Handles 403/400/500 scenarios.

logical_components.title: EmailNotificationStep
logical_components.description: Asynchronous step to send a welcome email to a newly created user containing credentials.
logical_components.business_logic: Sends a templated password delivery email after user creation. Builds a success payload including user fields and handles DB/HTTP errors with layered error handling. Notes security considerations about plaintext passwords in email and responses.

logical_components.title: Admin Create Admin Endpoint
logical_components.description: POST /admin/create_admin endpoint that creates a new admin (superuser) from admin-provided data, enforcing admin-only access and proper validation.
logical_components.business_logic: Performs an Authorization check to ensure the requester is a superuser, validates data.plan, checks for email duplication, hashes the password, constructs a new User with is_superuser=True and total_scans=0, persists it, and commits. Returns success data; may trigger optional notifications and returns 403/400/500 on errors.

logical_components.title: Admin User Persistence Lifecycle
logical_components.description: Lifecycle steps for admin user creation: in-memory object construction, password hashing, and DB persistence with session management.
logical_components.business_logic: Constructs the in-memory admin user object (fields: email, hashed password, first_name, last_name, plan, is_superuser=True, total_scans=0), adds to session, commits, and refreshes to load DB-generated fields (e.g., id).
